mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has improved from -23.4% to -19.1% over four weeks, signaling gradual return to office routines. This sustained upward trend in workplace attendance will drive commuter retail spending, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 4.3 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES continues to decline or remains flat over the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to improve relative to the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has stabilized near +9-11% across all four weeks, indicating sustained home-based activity patterns. This persistent elevation signals consumer preference for home-centered consumption, which suppresses discretionary retail visits and keeps RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stable between 9.4% and 11.1% across all four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility drops below 5% or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points despite sustained residential elevation.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility has improved from -34.4% to -29.1% over four weeks, a 5.3-point gain. When transit recovery exceeds 4 percentage points week-on-week, it signals sufficient commuter confidence to support retail foot traffic, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the subsequent four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves more than 4 percentage points in any single week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 5.3 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility reverses by more than 3 percentage points in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC remains below -20% despite transit gains.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility declined sharply from -16.0% (t-2w) to -23.0% (t-1w), then recovered to -15.3% (t-0w). This volatility in outdoor recreation signals consumer uncertainty about activity safety. When PARKS volatility exceeds 7 percentage points, consumers redirect discretionary spending away from retail, suppressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS week-on-week change exceeds 7 percentage points in magnitude
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS swung 7.7 points from t-2w to t-1w
failure_condition: PARKS stabilizes within a 3-point band and RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has remained stable and near-baseline (-3.4% to -6.0%), indicating consistent essential shopping. When essential shopping remains stable while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve together, consumers gain confidence to increase discretionary retail visits, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM variance < 3 percentage points AND WORKPLACES improves > 3 points AND TRANSIT improves > 3 points
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM range is only 2.6 points across four weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM drops below -8% or WORKPLACES/TRANSIT reverse their gains, and RETAIL_REC fails to improve.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility at -29.1% (t-0w) remains severely depressed, indicating ongoing transport restrictions or low commuter confidence. When TRANSIT remains below -25%, retail districts remain inaccessible to commuters, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed regardless of other activity signals over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -25% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -29.1% in t-0w, below -25% threshold for entire observation period
failure_condition: TRANSIT improves above -20% within two weeks and RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown a modest upward trend from -26.4% (t-3w) to -23.7% (t-0w), a 2.7-point improvement. This consistent week-on-week recovery signal, absent any reversal, indicates seasonal or policy-driven reopening momentum that will continue lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 2.7 points from t-3w to t-0w with no week-on-week decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines by more than 2 percentage points in any single week over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL elevation (+9.4%) combined with RETAIL_REC depression (-23.7%) and PARKS volatility indicates consumers are risk-averse and home-centered. When RESIDENTIAL exceeds +8% AND RETAIL_REC remains below -20%, consumer confidence is too low to support retail recovery, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL > +8% AND RETAIL_REC < -20% AND PARKS volatility > 5 points
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at +9.4%, RETAIL_REC at -23.7%, PARKS range 7.7 points
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL drops below +5% or RETAIL_REC improves above -15% within two weeks, indicating confidence recovery.
